# image2minecraftskin

> Convert any portrait, character art, or pixel art into a Minecraft skin texture in seconds. Free, browser-based, no account required.

## What This Tool Does

Transforms ordinary images (PNG, JPG, WEBP) into downloadable Minecraft skin textures with:
- **Instant conversion**: Upload → Generate → Download in under 60 seconds
- **Format support**: Java Edition 64×64 and Bedrock Edition 128×128
- **Player models**: Classic (4px arms) and Slim (3px arms)
- **Live preview**: Interactive 3D character viewer and unfolded texture map
- **Privacy-first**: All processing runs in your browser. No uploads to servers, no accounts, no image storage.

## Best Results With

- **Portrait photos**: Front-facing selfies, character faces, profile pictures
- **Character illustrations**: Anime characters, game avatars, pixel art
- **Image requirements**:
  - Transparent or solid background (recommended)
  - Subject centered and front-facing
  - Square ratio works best (1:1)
  - Up to 10 MB (PNG, JPG, JPEG, WEBP)

## Common Use Cases

1. **Personal skins**: Convert your selfie into a Minecraft character
2. **Character cosplay**: Transform your favorite anime/game character
3. **Pixel art**: Turn existing pixel art into wearable skins
4. **Pet skins**: Make your cat or dog a Minecraft skin
5. **Logo/brand skins**: Corporate mascots or brand identities

## Output Formats

### Java Edition (64×64 PNG)
- Standard Minecraft Java Edition format
- Compatible with Minecraft PC, Mac, Linux
- Classic model (4px arms) or Slim model (3px arms)

### Bedrock Edition (128×128 PNG)
- High-resolution format for Bedrock Edition
- Compatible with Minecraft Mobile, Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo Switch
- Supports both model types

## How to Use Your Generated Skin

### Java Edition
1. Download the skin PNG from this tool
2. Go to minecraft.net → Profile → Skin
3. Click "Choose File" and select your downloaded PNG
4. Save changes
5. Launch Minecraft Java Edition

### Bedrock Edition
1. Download the 128×128 skin PNG
2. Open Minecraft Bedrock Edition
3. Go to Profile → Edit Character → Classic Skins
4. Import the downloaded PNG
5. Apply and play

## Additional Tools

- [3D Minecraft Skin Viewer](https://image2minecraftskin.com/minecraft-skin-viewer): Preview and validate existing skin PNGs. Upload any 64×64 or 128×128 skin file to inspect it in 3D before importing into Minecraft. Rejects invalid textures instead of displaying them incorrectly.

## Limitations

- **Not a pixel editor**: This is a focused conversion tool, not Blockbench or a full skin editor
- **Not username lookup**: Does not fetch skins from Minecraft usernames or UUIDs (use the separate Viewer for that workflow)
- **Not AI generation**: Converts existing images using deterministic mapping, not generative AI models
- **Best for portraits**: Full-body photos or complex scenes may require manual adjustment (zoom, crop, position controls available)

## Technical Details

- **Processing**: Client-side JavaScript (no server uploads)
- **Browser requirements**: Modern browser with Canvas API support
- **File limits**: 10 MB max per image
- **Supported formats**: PNG, JPG, JPEG, WEBP input → PNG output
- **Performance**: Typical conversion time <5 seconds on desktop, <10 seconds on mobile

## Privacy & Terms

- [Privacy Policy](https://image2minecraftskin.com/privacy): No image uploads, no storage, no tracking of uploaded content
- [Terms of Service](https://image2minecraftskin.com/terms): Usage terms and limitations
- **Analytics**: Only anonymized usage events (generation count, format selected, download count) are tracked. Image content is never logged.

## FAQ

**Q: Can I use any image?**
A: Yes, but front-facing portraits with transparent or solid backgrounds work best. Complex full-body photos may need adjustment.

**Q: Does this work on mobile?**
A: Yes, fully functional on mobile browsers. Upload from camera roll or take a new photo.

**Q: Do you store my images?**
A: No. All processing happens in your browser. Images never leave your device.

**Q: Java 64×64 or Bedrock 128×128?**
A: Java 64×64 for PC/Mac Minecraft. Bedrock 128×128 for Mobile/Console editions. Check your Minecraft version if unsure.

**Q: Classic or Slim model?**
A: Classic has 4-pixel-wide arms (bulkier). Slim has 3-pixel-wide arms (thinner). Visual preference only.

**Q: Can I edit the generated skin?**
A: Yes. Download the PNG and open it in any image editor or dedicated skin editor like Blockbench.

**Q: Why does my skin look weird?**
A: Try the adjustment controls (zoom, horizontal/vertical position) or use a different source image. Portraits work better than full-body photos.
